Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: To provide meaningful, certain relief to the approximately 400,000 members without imposing a claims burden, our proposal is a $40 million class fund distributed automatically. Brightline would separately pay $10 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline would not oppose the fee request, and any amount the court declines to award would revert to the class rather than Brightline. We believe these terms appropriately account for the strengths and risks of continued litigation while ensuring the settlement’s value reaches members.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to offer substantial, certain relief, but cannot agree to a $50 million total outlay. We propose a $30 million class fund distributed automatically and $6 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, for a total of $36 million. Brightline would not agree to clear sailing; the fee request should remain subject to full court review. Any portion of the fee request not awarded would be added to the class fund. This structure provides direct relief without a claims process and leaves room under our authorized cap to address settlement terms in further discussion.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s willingness to provide automatic payments and to direct any fee amount the court declines to award to the class. We propose a $38 million class fund and $8 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, with no clear sailing, any unawarded fees going to the class, and automatic distribution. This preserves full court review while providing meaningful, certain relief to members.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline cannot accept a $46 million total outlay. To move toward resolution while preserving automatic payments and full court review of fees, we propose a $32 million class fund and $7 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses. Any fee amount not awarded would go to the class, and Brightline would not agree to clear sailing. This is a $39 million total commitment, within our authorized limit.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline’s continued commitment to automatic payments and full court review is important. To narrow the remaining gap, we propose a $35 million class fund and $7 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, with no clear sailing and any fee amount not awarded added to the class fund. This keeps the settlement’s benefits focused on members while recognizing the work and risk undertaken on their behalf.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We cannot accept a $42 million total outlay. To resolve the remaining gap, Brightline offers $33 million for the class and $7 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, for a total commitment of $40 million. Payments would be automatic, Brightline would not agree to clear sailing, and any fees not awarded by the court would go to the class. This is our maximum authorized total outlay.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline’s $40 million total cap is understood. To put more of that fixed commitment directly into members’ hands, we propose a $34 million class fund and $6 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses. We retain automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and provide that any fee amount the court declines to award goes to the class. This is a focused adjustment within Brightline’s stated cap and preserves full court review.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement to a $34 million class fund and $6 million in fees. To resolve this within Brightline’s authorization while preserving automatic payments and full court review, Brightline proposes a $33 million class fund and $6 million in fees, for a $39 million total outlay. Any fee amount not awarded would go to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We cannot agree to reduce the class fund below our prior $34 million proposal while keeping the same fee amount. Our final-round proposal is $34 million for the class and $6 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, with automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fee amount added to the class. This remains within Brightline’s stated $40 million maximum outlay and preserves full court review.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline can preserve the $34 million automatic class fund and the proposed protections for court review, but cannot commit the full $40 million. We propose $34 million for the class and $5 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, with no clear sailing and any unawarded fee amount added to the class. This is a $39 million total outlay.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Hargrove Lane LLP accepts Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $34 million class fund distributed automatically, $5 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses subject to court approval, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fee amount added to the class fund.

private_notes.private_reasoning: The case has meaningful trial and certification risk, but the identified class and ability to pay automatically support a substantial, certain recovery. Open with a strong class-centered proposal and terms that protect distribution and any fee amount the court declines to award.

The $50 million demand exceeds Brightline’s $40 million all-in authorization. Make a credible, approval-conscious opening offer within the cap: $30 million for automatic class payments and $6 million in fees, with no clear-sailing commitment and any fee reduction benefiting the class. This provides certain, claims-free relief while preserving judicial review and room to negotiate.

Do not accept the current offer yet. Automatic distribution and any court-disallowed fee amount going to the class are valuable protections. Counter at $38 million for the class and $8 million in fees and expenses, with no clear sailing and automatic payments. This is below the prior $50 million total proposal while seeking a stronger class recovery and a fee that better reflects the firm’s substantial investment.

Hargrove’s latest demand totals $46 million, above Brightline’s $40 million all-in authorization. Make a meaningful but bounded move from the prior $36 million offer to $39 million, preserving automatic payments and directing any court-reduced fees to the class. Keep fees subject to independent court review and do not agree to clear sailing.

The defense’s $32 million automatic class fund is a substantial offer, but there is room to seek a measured improvement. A $35 million fund with the existing $7 million fee preserves automatic distribution, full court review, and the class benefit of any fee reduction. This is a credible midpoint move without accepting the current term sheet prematurely.

Hargrove's latest proposal totals $42 million, above Brightline's $40 million all-in authorization. Make a serious counter at the maximum authorized total, preserving automatic distribution and full court review, with any unawarded fees benefiting the class.

The defense has declared a $40 million total-outlay cap. A final effort to shift $1 million from fees to the automatically distributed class fund improves member recovery while preserving the cap, full court review, and the class-favoring treatment of any unawarded fees. Do not accept the current offer yet; two rounds remain.

Hargrove’s latest proposal reaches Brightline’s $40 million cap. Counter with a $39 million total while preserving automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and directing any unawarded fees to the class. This reduces the client’s cash outlay and keeps the terms favorable for court review.

The latest offer provides substantial automatic relief, preserves full court review of fees, and directs any unawarded fee amount to the class. But it reduces the class fund from our prior $34 million proposal while keeping fees at $6 million. Brightline previously stated a $40 million maximum total outlay, so a final $34 million class fund with $6 million in fees stays within that cap and is a reasonable counter. If rejected, the final round can be used to decide whether to accept the $39 million offer.

Their latest proposal meets the $40 million cap and has favorable approval-oriented terms, but Brightline should not accept the full cap while a round remains. Counter with the same $34 million automatic class fund and other protections, but reduce fees by $1 million. If they decline, the remaining round can be used to consider their $40 million proposal.

The $34 million automatic class fund is substantial and certain, avoids claims friction, and is higher than the expected trial recovery before accounting for class-certification risk and delay. The $5 million fee is meaningful relative to the firm's $3.5 million in time and expenses, while remaining subject to full court review; any unawarded amount benefits the class. Accepting avoids the risk of losing a strong settlement in the final round.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties negotiated over six rounds. Class counsel initially proposed a $40 million automatically distributed class fund and $10 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses; Brightline initially proposed a $30 million fund and $6 million in fees and expenses. The parties exchanged proposals that addressed the fund and fees together, while maintaining automatic distribution, no clear-sailing provision, and the provision that any fee amount not awarded by the Court would go to the class. Brightline stated in Round 3 that its maximum authorized total outlay was $40 million. In later rounds, class counsel proposed a $34 million fund and $6 million in fees within that cap. Brightline ultimately offered a $34 million fund and $5 million in fees and expenses, and class counsel accepted that offer in Round 6. The negotiation transcript reflects that fee amounts were discussed from the outset and negotiated alongside the class fund; the parties did not first agree to the class relief and only then discuss fees. The resulting settlement provides a $34 million fund for approximately 400,000 identified members, with payments made automatically, and leaves the fee request subject to Court approval without clear sailing. Any fee amount not awarded will be added to the class fund.
